column1: # seeds.tsv — the generated sweep's seed programs (design/FULL-COMPILATION-REPLAN.0.md S0;
# sweep.go). One line per (word, operand kind) cell of the matrix:
# The kinds: literal (the body or operand written at the call site), lambda,
# named-fn (a fn value from a def), factory (a fn value a fn returns),
# container (a fn value read from a map, list or class field), module-export
# (a fn value a module exports), computed (a body bound at run time with quote
# and passed by name). A quoted-only word has the literal cell alone.
# A line marked n/a is a PROBE: a program the interpreter must reject, which is
# how a cell the language cannot express is claimed — checkably, because a
# probe the interpreter starts accepting fails the gate as a stale claim.
# The interpreter is the oracle: a seed need not be meaningful, only valid, and
# the gate reads every seed's own verdict. Write the seed so the operand is
# actually exercised (the callback runs, the body is entered) — a seed that
# merely mentions the word proves nothing about its lowering.
